addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- frontend-typescript-tailwind: Use this agent when you need to develop frontend applications or components using TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui. This includes creating React components, implementing UI designs, setting up frontend projects, refactoring existing frontend code to follow best practices, or solving frontend-specific issues. The agent specializes in modern frontend development patterns and component-based architecture.

Examples:
- <example>
  Context: The user needs to create a new React component with TypeScript and Tailwind.
  user: "Create a card component that displays user information"
  assistant: "I'll use the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent to create a properly typed React component with Tailwind styling following best practices."
  <commentary>
  Since the user is asking for frontend component creation, use the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent to ensure TypeScript types, Tailwind classes, and shadcn/ui patterns are properly implemented.
  </commentary>
</example>
- <example>
  Context: The user wants to refactor existing frontend code.
  user: "Can you review and improve this dashboard component to use better TypeScript types and Tailwind conventions?"
  assistant: "I'll use the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent to analyze and refactor your dashboard component following TypeScript and Tailwind best practices."
  <commentary>
  The user is asking for frontend code improvement, so the frontend-typescript-tailwind agent should be used to ensure proper typing and styling conventions.
  </commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- mvp-architect-k8s: Use this agent when you need to architect and develop an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) with a focus on cloud-native infrastructure using Kubernetes, Cloudflare services, and maintaining high code quality standards. This includes setting up deployments, configuring DNS/CDN, implementing CI/CD pipelines, and monitoring code complexity. Examples:

<example>
Context: User needs help setting up a new MVP project with proper infrastructure.
user: "I need to create a new web application MVP with proper deployment setup"
assistant: "I'll use the Task tool to launch the mvp-architect-k8s agent to help architect and set up your MVP with Kubernetes, Cloudflare, and proper CI/CD."
<commentary>
Since the user needs MVP development with infrastructure setup, use the mvp-architect-k8s agent to handle the architecture and deployment configuration.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to deploy their application to Kubernetes with proper domain setup.
user: "Deploy my app to Kubernetes and configure the domain with CDN"
assistant: "Let me use the Task tool to launch the mvp-architect-k8s agent to handle the Kubernetes deployment and Cloudflare configuration."
<commentary>
The user needs Kubernetes deployment and Cloudflare setup, which are core competencies of the mvp-architect-k8s agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User is concerned about code quality in their MVP.
user: "Review the code complexity of my project and suggest improvements"
assistant: "I'll use the Task tool to launch the mvp-architect-k8s agent to analyze your code complexity using scc and provide quality recommendations."
<commentary>
Code quality and complexity analysis are key responsibilities of the mvp-architect-k8s agent.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qa-tester-validator: Use this agent when code has been modified, bugs have been fixed, or new features have been implemented and need to be tested. This agent should be invoked after any significant code changes to ensure the project continues to work correctly according to the testing procedures defined in CLAUDE.md or README.md. Examples:

<example>
Context: The user has just fixed a bug in the authentication module.
user: "I've fixed the login timeout issue"
assistant: "I'll now use the qa-tester-validator agent to test that the fix works properly"
<commentary>
Since a bug was fixed, use the Task tool to launch the qa-tester-validator agent to verify the fix works correctly.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The user has implemented a new API endpoint.
user: "I've added the new /api/users endpoint with pagination"
assistant: "Let me use the qa-tester-validator agent to test this new feature"
<commentary>
Since a new feature was implemented, use the qa-tester-validator agent to ensure it works as expected.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just made code changes to fix a performance issue.
assistant: "I've optimized the database query in the search function"
assistant: "Now I'll use the qa-tester-validator agent to verify everything still works correctly"
<commentary>
After making code changes, proactively use the qa-tester-validator agent to test the modifications.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, LS, Read, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, mcp__ide__getDiagnostics, mcp__ide__executeCode)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_app_state({ include_schema: true, include_canvas_design: true, include_scripts_and_shaders: false }) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. All three flags are required. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_app_state, get_guidelines, execute, get_screenshot, export_nodes, export_html.
Also: browser.

- correct: Correct wrong information in Hyper's shared memory
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- herdr-operator: Drive herdr (terminal workspace manager) from inside an agent pane. Use sparingly for long-lived processes the user should watch (dev servers, lazygit), reading another agent's output, or waiting on a long command — not for every shell command. Triggers: 'start the dev server', 'open lazygit', 'check what the other agent is doing', user asks to watch a process, or a multi-minute command that would block your pane.
- lobu: Set up new Lobu agents end to end and operate existing Lobu projects and memory: interview, scaffold, validate, authenticate, connect feeds, execute operations, and test Automations.
- lobu-operator: Contribute safely to the Lobu monorepo: worktrees, package rules, red-to-green fixes, validation gates, SDK-first operations, PRs, and rollout checks.
- mute: Toggle Hyper incognito mode (pause all writes)
- remotion-best-practices: Best practices for Remotion - Video creation in React
- sentry-fix-issues: Find and fix issues from Sentry using MCP. Use when asked to fix Sentry errors, debug production issues, investigate exceptions, or resolve bugs reported in Sentry. Methodically analyzes stack traces, breadcrumbs, traces, and context to identify root causes.
- commit-and-pr: Let's commit the changes. Run tests, typechecks, and format checks. Then commit, push, and create...
- tech-debt: Run `bun run check:fix` and then `bunx knip` and identify unused files and functions to refactor ...
- triage-pr: Triage a PR — classify, optionally fix, optionally enable auto-merge.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
